run.market_summary: 1) Fed may have to hike: the hot October CPI has rates traders pricing a December hike and possibly a series of hikes (WSJ: 'bigger and faster rate rises'). The dollar is at a 19-month high and gold has fallen to $3,973, but stocks have barely adjusted (SPY -0.9%, QQQ -0.2% over 5 days). 2) Chip export controls are tightening during an Nvidia governance crisis: the Jensen Huang alleged-spy scandal has revived China chip-curb pressure ahead of the Trump-Xi summit, and the US is widening AI chip controls to seven nations. NVDA is down 13% in 5 days, but money has rotated into AMD and chip-equipment names (+6-13%) instead of leaving the sector. 3) Oil news points both ways: OPEC+ output rose about 2M bpd and Brent is below $90, while Israel is preparing a possible strike on Iran. No clean trade there.

ideas.thesis: Hot October CPI has headlines pointing to a 'larger series of rate hikes' and the Fed being 'forced to confront case for bigger and faster rate rises', yet TLT is only down 1% in 5 days. It is the cleanest expression of the hawkish repricing.

The Huang scandal has revived China chip-curb pressure ahead of the Trump-Xi summit, and the US is widening AI export controls to seven nations and pressing South Korea. Chip-equipment makers with large China revenue are the most direct target, and LRCX is up 6.5% in 5 days on the rotation away from Nvidia.

Rate markets now price a possible December Fed hike after the hot CPI, but QQQ is roughly flat on the week. Its long-duration tech names are also exposed to the AI leadership turmoil ('Nasdaq futures drop as Nvidia leads decline in AI-related shares').

analysis.headline: Two things moved markets: Nvidia gapped down 13% after Jensen Huang resigned and buyers recovered most of it, then a Treasury selloff took the 10-year to 5.10%, worsened midday by Trump's Iran remarks and the oil jump that followed. That pushed gold, bitcoin and small caps lower while the S&P barely moved.
analysis.narrative:
The day had two parts. Before the open, Nvidia was the story. After-hours reports on Wednesday said the board might oust Huang, and he resigned around 9am ET, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO. NVDA opened down 13%, SMH down 4.3%, XLK down 2.6% and QQQ down 1.5%. Dip buyers stepped in hard (NVDA volume 4.4x, record retail buying) and money moved into rivals: AVGO +5.5% and AMD up about 5-6%. NVDA rallied 10% off the open to close -4.3%, and QQQ/XLK finished nearly flat. On the index tape, the Nvidia shock was mostly absorbed.

The second part was rates, and it explains the broad weakness: only 1 of 13 sectors rose, and nearly every non-tech sector lost 0.5-1.4% after the open. Treasuries reopened after Veterans Day and repriced to the hot Oct-10 CPI and hawkish Fed comments (Goolsbee, Daly, Hammack). The 10-year gapped up 6bp. Midday, Trump posted that "we don't need a deal with Iran." Oil turned from flat to +2.8% intraday, the selloff sped up (10-year about 5.12% at the high, 30-year about 5.44%), and European bonds followed (WSJ 15:53). TLT fell 1.5% (z -2.0) and TIP fell too, so real yields rose. Gold dropped 3% to a one-year low near $3,850-3,877 (z -2.0) on higher real yields and a firmer dollar. Small caps (IWM -1.6%), materials, staples, health care and real estate all faded during the session. Jobless claims came in at 200k vs 195k expected, a little soft, and did nothing to stop the bond selloff.

Other unusual moves: BABA fell 7% (z -3.1) and KWEB 3.2%. Reports that Megaspeed moved $7.5bn of Nvidia chips into China, plus the coming Commerce rule to block remote access to AI chips, raised fears that Chinese AI firms will lose access to compute. The Hang Seng fell 1.3% with Alibaba leading. Bitcoin lost 3.3% and broke below $72k and its 200-day average, hit by hawkish Fed bets and ETF outflows. IBIT (z -2.0), MSTR (-6.5%; Yahoo said MSCI will drop it from two indexes), COIN and HOOD all opened sharply lower. Higher oil helped energy (XLE +1.5%, OXY, XOM) and hurt airlines (JETS -3.8%; JetBlue -5%, UAL and DAL about -4%). The VIX rose only 7% to about 18.7 (z 0.4), so this was a repricing of rates and single names, not panic.

-3.1% to a one-year low near $3,850-3,877 as real yields rose and the dollar firmed on December hike bets.

Opened +1% on Blackstone's up-to-$1.5B co-funding deal for berobenatide, then fell 3% during the session along with defensive health care. Also, Reuters reported it will stop selling Premarin in Canada.
+1.5%: oil rose during the session after Trump's Iran remarks.

analysis.cross_asset_read: This was a rates shock, not a fear shock. The 10-year rose 10bp to 5.10% and TIP fell, so real yields were up. The dollar gained 0.24%, gold fell 3% and bitcoin fell 3%, which fits a hawkish-Fed read, while the VIX barely moved (+7% to about 18.7). Oil up with airlines down shows a real energy impulse in the afternoon, and it fed into breakevens and long-end yields. Tech recovered during the session (SMH +3.5% from the open) while non-tech fell, so the Nvidia story was mostly a single-name event that dip buyers absorbed. The broad weakness came from yields: small caps, materials, rate-sensitive sectors and defensives were the losers. The morning's 'Oil Edges Lower' framing was overtaken by the afternoon oil spike.

axis_realized.note: Bonds reopened after the holiday into hike pricing; Daly, Goolsbee and Hammack were hawkish. TLT -1.5%, 10-year 5.10%, gold at a one-year low, IWM -1.6%.
Curb fears hit China AI names (BABA -7%, KWEB -3.2%) more than US equipment makers (LRCX about -0.9%).
Trump's 'no need for an Iran deal' post and Israeli strike preparations lifted oil during the session and added to the bond selloff.
Crude +2.8% during the session despite OPEC+ adding 2M bpd; XLE up, JETS -3.8%.

model_grade.summary: Strong on the main call. Hawkish policy was the day's biggest driver and the SHORT TLT idea was the best trade. The model was right about chip-curb pressure but put it in the wrong names, and it got oil the wrong way (leaned looser; oil rose on Iran rhetoric). All three short ideas made money in absolute terms, but SHORT QQQ was flat against SPY because tech recovered from the Nvidia gap while rate-sensitive small caps fell more.
got_right: SHORT TLT +1.48% (+1.13% vs SPY): the cleanest expression of the day.
chip_export_controls +0.52: curb fears were real and drove BABA/KWEB lower.
geopolitical_conflict +0.20 was the right direction (Israel-Iran, Trump's Iran comments).
SHORT LRCX +0.89% (+0.54% vs SPY): small gain.
got_wrong: energy_supply -0.19: oil rose 2.8% during the session; Iran rhetoric outweighed the OPEC+ supply headlines.
SHORT QQQ: only +0.32%, -0.03% vs SPY. Nasdaq recovered 1.2% from the open as dip buyers and the AVGO/AMD rotation absorbed the Nvidia shock; small caps were the better rate short.
missed: That Huang would actually resign, and that a -13% gap would be bought back to -4%.
The China ADR channel for chip curbs (BABA z -3.1) was a better expression than US equipment shorts.
Crypto breakdown: BTC below its 200-day, IBIT z -2, MSTR hit by MSCI removal.
The midday Trump Iran post that drove oil higher, airlines lower and the bond selloff faster.
That cash Treasuries were reopening after Veterans Day, which meant catch-up selling.

lessons: Price in holiday catch-up: when the cash bond market was closed the day before, expect TLT to absorb two days of news at once. That would have raised conviction in SHORT TLT.

Express a hawkish-Fed theme through IWM, gold or BTC rather than QQQ when a megacap-tech story dominates the tape: tech flows are idiosyncratic, while small caps and gold respond cleanly to real yields.
Map chip-export-control scores to Chinese AI buyers (BABA, KWEB) as well as US equipment makers. Today BABA fell about 7x as much as LRCX.

Don't let scheduled OPEC supply data outweigh live US-Iran rhetoric in energy_supply. When geopolitical_conflict is positive, cap how negative energy_supply can go and consider a long-crude/short-JETS pair.
For a governance shock known before the open at a heavily owned megacap, add a 'fade the gap' rule: on very high volume with record retail buying, the open tends to be the low.
Track scheduled index events (MSCI's Nov 11 list) for crypto proxies such as MSTR.
